entries.verbatim: YES, all three directions, as a duty the strategy already states (§4: a mark on the close verse is corroboration to disclose; a mark with no formula is disclosed and never cuts alone) and the both-sides law requires for the onset seam. Each disclosure names the verse, the mark type, single-witness, and its direction (at the onset seam / interior / at the close seam). The measured gap is 27 interior marks (22 rows), 30 close-seam marks and 27 onset-seam marks whose verse the row never names; the union is about 57 rows. FORM: a boundary_evidence_refs entry per mark with an annotation of at most six words drawn from at least four rotating formulations (so no seven-word run can form), plus one clause of prose only where the mark bears on an argument. TOOL: check_marks' symmetry arm is extended to all three directions and to rows that cite no marks at all, and its false_mark_absence_claim scope adopts the vocabulary below. VOCABULARY (binding for rows and the validator): 'inside the span' means recorded on verses first..last-1; a mark recorded on the LAST verse is 'at the close seam', not inside; a mark on the verse before the first verse is 'at the onset seam'. Under that vocabulary the rows P03-015, P09-002, P11-001, P11-002, P11-008, P11-009, P11-013, P02-002, P02-005 flagged false_mark_absence_claim are TRUE claims and the flags are validator false positives; P05-004 and P05-008 (TRIAGE-EZ-02) are real onset-seam gaps.

SPAN-COVERAGE governs: a row discloses every K/Q verse its span covers, naming the verse (pmarks kq_note and strategy §8 both state it, and 55 of 59 covering rows do it). Locality is NOT required: a disclosure anywhere in the row satisfies a quotation binding to that verse; the suite's prose_dual warn (9 rows) is advisory and is not a defect. Fixes: P08-002, P11-004, P11-007, P11-014 add the disclosure; P04-009 (21:28), P07-001 (29:4), P07-009 (30:16), P07-006 (31:5), P08-007 (35:12), P11-002 (44:5), P11-010 (47:8) name the covered verse they omit. P05-003's 'No paseq or K/Q sites inside 22:23-31' is TRUE against pmarks (ch 22's only K/Q is 22:18) — the validator's kq_claim flag at 22:23 is a false positive to be answered as such.

Count-only at verse granularity, per SPAN, as the practised convention (63 of 69 covering rows disclose it): a row states that paseq is recorded on N verses of its span or names them; never a position. There is NO per-occurrence enumeration duty — a paseq is intra-verse and cannot bear on a seam, so under-enumeration (OL c22's third of occurrences) is not a defect and is not repaired. The 6 silent rows (P08-007, P08-010, P08-014, P11-010, P11-011, P11-015) add the count-only disclosure. A comma-placed 'count-only, single-witness' is a qualifier, not a denial; the rewording rule does not reach it. A row that DENIES paseq in its span must be true (none of the 69 covering rows carries a denial pattern).

SCOPE: the rule reaches every absence claim about a checkable layer (mark, K/Q, paseq, puncta, dateline, editorial note, formula device) that is APPENDED behind a comma to a clause whose head is a different claim, or set off parenthetically inside a positive claim (P07-008's 'held, then not resolved' shape). Its rationale is machine-checkability: the toolkit's checkers cannot bind a denial that sits outside its clause. A COORDINATE CHAIN consisting solely of absence claims over one named span ('no K/Q note, no paseq, no parashah mark and no editorial note lie within this span') is NOT a hidden denial: each item shares the verb and the scope and the checker's absence-phrase arm reads it; it PASSES. BAND: LOW when every denied fact is true and no boundary rests on the denial (form only); MEDIUM when a denied fact is false or the denial carries the seam; never HIGH on form alone. Consequences for landed verdicts (the peers apply them): OL c21's two medium comma-placed dateline denials with true facts move to LOW; LF c22's two low challenges on pure coordinate chains become supports; OL c16's chains pass; OL c01's device-classification denials in P01-002, P01-005, P01-006 are scored LOW each only if of the appended shape; OL c13's 26:19 label is reworded only if the denial is appended to a positive claim.

By CONTENT above a threshold: a run of five or more consecutive words identical to the WEB text at the cited or covered verse is a WEB quotation whatever its delimiter, and must carry the double curly quotes and an in-field web: reference; a run of one to four words in straight single quotes is a gloss (a literal rendering of plain prose coincides with the translation at that length). Inside a WEB quotation the bytes are WEB's, apostrophe glyph included; a straight apostrophe there is a LOW form defect corrected wherever the row is touched, and no corpus-wide glyph normalisation is ordered. TOOL: check_web_quotes is extended to straight-quoted and unquoted runs at the five-word threshold and to byte-compare apostrophes. Instances: the c19 renderings at MT 40:28 (11 words), 40:4 (10) and 40:48 (9) are quotations and are delimited and referenced or rewritten as paraphrase; the c21 short phrases and P09-010's 39:29 gloss are measured against the threshold by the peers.

CLOSED as written: strategy §6 grants the 14-16 allowance to 'the measured and listed blocks (40-42, 45, 48)' only. Every other row measures its length against the 7-10 target; a complete formula-bounded unit longer than the target is disclosed as over the target and is not 'over a cap', and this ruling sets no confidence rule by length (the E-02 whole-chapter posture stands unchanged). Wording fixes, no seam and no confidence change, on the rows that cite the allowance outside its scope: P01-001, P01-008, P01-009, P01-014, P04-001, P04-008, P05-004, P06-009, P07-006, P11-003, P11-007 (P10-008 in ch 41 is inside it). 'The span would exceed every cap' is a FALSE ground — the ruled posture admits whole-chapter and long spans at reduced confidence with the cap disclosed — and is replaced by the content ground the row already has in P01-013 and P11-012.

YES, by one step: when a mark is recorded on the verse before a rejected cut, the strongest_rejected_alternative field must NAME the mark and weigh it as corroboration for the alternative; a disclosure in device_notes alone is insufficient, and a re-argued rejection is not required. Marks never cut alone, so the rejection may stand on the text signals it already names. P01-008 (4:3) and P01-014 (7:22) are checked for this in the author wave.

TEXT governs (contract: boundary-driving evidence is text signals only; parashot are weak corroboration). The witness's division is disclosed as corroboration for the alternative and stated as continuity evidence against the row where it conflicts; it is never resolved by inverting a mark's direction (the 14:1 case). The ch-7 shape (witness 7:1-4 / 7:5-22 / 7:23-27 against the corpus 7:5-9 / 7:10-27) is a legitimate seam question for peer_01, decided on text evidence with the witness division as the disclosed alternative.

The schema has one strongest_rejected_alternative; it holds the strongest. Any further live interior candidate is disclosed in one clause of device_notes as weighed and not taken, with the device that would carry it named. No new field. Whether 13:14/13:15 is the strongest alternative for that row is the peer's call.

**CONF-CAL — what confidence measures** (binding, ruling #e13):

> Confidence records the strength of the **boundary evidence**, not the quality of the row's prose (which you are
> repairing), not size conformance where the strategy licenses the size, and not a genre hold the strategy
> licenses with disclosure.
>
> - **HIGH** — both seams two-faced (a licensed text signal on the near face and a text signal — onset, close or
>   scene change — on the far face) and no rival seam licensed under CUT-RULE. A mark-only or paragraph-grade
>   rival is weighed under A9/A16, **never fatal**.
> - **MEDIUM** — both seams carry a licensed near-face signal but one far face carries only a mark or nothing,
>   **OR** a two-faced rival is held on stated grounds.
> - **MEDIUM_LOW** — a seam whose near-face signal is itself weak (mid-verse formula; discourse turn without
>   formula) with an empty far face, or a region §7 holds without bespoke rationale.
> - **LOW** — a seam without a licensed text signal, or where the strategy directs low.
>
> §7's direction is the tie-breaker where it names the region. **No row's confidence is raised unasked.**

**#e14 Q2 refines the MEDIUM_LOW limb** and you must apply the refinement, not the bare phrase:

> "Mid-verse formula (weak)" means a close formula followed **within the verse, after the major disjunctive, by
> an INDEPENDENT clause** not syntactically dependent on the formula's own clause. A formula whose remaining
> words are a **dependent completion** of its clause — temporal infinitive, adverbial, relative — is verse-final
> in effect and grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal.

So 29:9 (recognition formula ends at the etnachta, an independent causal clause fills the second half) is the
weak shape; 36:23 (the recognition clause runs to the silluq with the formula tokens embedded) is **not**.

entries.id: CUT-RULE, limb (a), limb (b), and the precedence of a driver over a mark
entries.verbatim:
## 1. CUT-RULE — the messenger and *ve'attah* second limb

The strategy states this rule three ways. **ONE formulation governs** (ruling #e13):

> A messenger formula is a **sub-onset** when
> **(a)** the addressee changes, **or**
> **(b)** the verse immediately before it **ENDS on** a close-role formula (utterance or recognition, any
> inventoried or D3 variant) — **VERSE-FINAL, not mid-verse**.
>
> **A mark alone never satisfies limb (b).** Strategy lines 322-323 are an incomplete summary, not a third rule.
>
> The same two limbs govern **"and you, son of man"** (*ve'attah*) inside an already-open unit: it is a sub-onset
> when the addressee changes or the unit has closed on a verse-final close-role formula before it. A **renewed
> command to the same addressee after a verse-final UTTERANCE signature is a paragraph**, not an onset.

**PRECEDENCE — a driver outranks a mark** (ruling #e13):

> A licensed text-signal driver (transport verb inside a vision, word-event, dateline, messenger/*ve'attah*
> sub-onset under CUT-RULE, refrain close) **outranks a closed-section boundary**, which is weak corroboration
> and is disclosed **for the alternative it corroborates**. The over-split guard — "a row under 3 verses only
> when it is a complete word-event unit" — then governs whether a licensed driver yields a row at all.

Note the direction in the second clause: a mark that supports the *rival* is disclosed as supporting the rival.
Do not write it up as if it supported the row.

## 5. The A9/A16 weighing duty

Where a rival seam exists, the row must **weigh** it, not ignore it and not merely mention it. A weighing says:
what the rival's near face carries, what its far face carries, whether CUT-RULE licenses it, and on what stated
ground the row holds against it. A licensed two-faced rival held on stated grounds is **MEDIUM** — that is
CONF-CAL's second limb, and it is a normal, defensible outcome, not a weakness to hide.

A rival you cannot weigh honestly is an escalation, not a rewrite.

verbatim.binding: for Ezekiel now; proposed to method section 17 as the cross-book definition
verbatim.1_argued_citation: Any verse anchor a prose field carries — an Ezek.C.V token with or without witness prefix, a bare C:V cite, an 'MT C:V' qualifier, or a v. / vv. / verse(s) N expression resolved against a single-chapter span — together with the assertion it anchors. Fields scanned: every string field except SKIP_KEYS (unchanged).
verbatim.2_unit: A dash-range is one citation; a comma / 'and' list is one citation per member; repeated citation of the same verse-set in one row is one citation.
verbatim.3_mirrored: A citation is mirrored when a boundary_evidence_refs entry covers its verse, or, for a range, covers either endpoint or the whole range, compared in WEB space after witness conversion.
verbatim.4_defect: Every unmirrored citation with at least one verse inside the A4 window [first-1, last+1] is a worklist item; a citation wholly outside the window is far-side: recorded, never a defect (#e12 A4).
verbatim.5_no_narrowing_to_evidentiary: 'Argued' is NOT narrowed to 'argued as evidence'. Under OW-18 a verse anchor is an assertion about the witness at that verse, and the refs list is the row's checkable index of such assertions; the rows already practise this (P07-001 mirrors 29:4 'not argued as boundary evidence'; P08-002 mirrors 33:20 'disclosed, never argued as a boundary'). The member judges mirroring; it never judges weight. Enforce in the tool what the tool can measure (OW-18); put the judgement where a person writes it and a reviewer reads it.
verbatim.6_role_token_mandatory: Every installed entry carries one fixed ROLE token, then free text under the rotation rule (at least 4 formulations, at most 6 words): WARRANT-onset | WARRANT-close | WARRANT-rival (the A9/A16 rival weighed) | WARRANT-absence-over-range (the 'no formula / mark / K-Q inside C:V-C:V' claims) | DISCLOSURE-kq | DISCLOSURE-mark | DISCLOSURE-paseq | DISCLOSURE-note | DISCLOSURE-device (an in-span device the boundary does not rest on) | QUOTE (an A6 run anchored here) | ANCHOR (a content or structural statement the boundary does not rest on; the rows' existing 'not argued as boundary evidence'). The token is what the spot wave checks: a WARRANT token on a verse the rationale does not rest on is a defect; an ANCHOR token is never a boundary claim. Existing entries are NOT re-tokenised in this wave; the vocabulary applies to installs.
verbatim.7_why_not_option_2: The member is a Tier-0 gate. Installing the peers' 47 and keeping the member 'as a net' leaves about 145 in-span citations flagging at the close gate unless the rule is changed — and the rule is A4, which R1 confirmed. An end state in which the gate is red and the worklist is done is not a choice; it is a deferred contradiction.
verbatim.8_why_not_narrowing: MEASURED above: the class a narrowing would remove is about five entries, and no mechanical test separates them from the Hebrew-quoted, rival-seam and absence claims around them without a judgement the tool cannot make (peer_11's A4 finding). The cost of the honest rule is a handful of ANCHOR entries; the cost of the narrowing is a tool that encodes a judgement it cannot audit.

entries.id: clause 6 v2 (near and far for a rival)

verbatim.face_qualifier_mandatory_on_warrants: WARRANT-onset, WARRANT-close and WARRANT-rival carry a face qualifier: ':near' (the seam verse inside the unit the seam bounds — the row's first verse for its onset, its last verse for its close, the candidate onset verse for a rival), ':far' (the adjacent verse across the seam), ':interior' (an in-span verse the warrant rests on that is neither — e.g. the מופת partner at 24:24 for the 24:27 close; permitted for WARRANT-close and WARRANT-onset only when the annotation names the device). Form: 'oshb:Ezek.33.20 [WARRANT-onset:far] pe-marked close behind the dateline'. For WARRANT-onset and WARRANT-close the member DERIVES the face from (verse, span) and FAILS LOUD on a mismatch, so the qualifier is verified, not free text. For WARRANT-rival the seam is not in the schema, so the annotation's first token names the seam pair — 'oshb:Ezek.33.12 [WARRANT-rival:near] 33.11/33.12 ve'attah, same audience, unlicensed' — and the member checks the ref's verse is one side of the pair and the qualifier matches that side.
verbatim.absence_tokens: WARRANT-absence (a single verse or a range; the boundary rests on the absence — 'no formula, mark, K/Q or paseq at C:V' or 'inside C:V-C:V') and DISCLOSURE-absence (a single verse or a range; recorded, the boundary does not rest on it — the honest home for 'device census records no stroke here'). WARRANT-absence-over-range is retained as a deprecated alias the member accepts and maps to WARRANT-absence. The citation sweep's mark, paseq and puncta arms treat any *-absence token as a NEGATED claim and verify the census is EMPTY at the verse(s): a false absence (device present) is a defect (Q6.2).
verbatim.worked_example_per_token: the author brief carries one worked example per token, including the three cases lane 01 found divergent: a verse with neither device nor mark that the rationale rests on (WARRANT with :near/:far, the ground named — content is a warrant when the rationale rests on it); an inventoried device the boundary does not rest on (DISCLOSURE-device, never ANCHOR); a device that is not recorded (never DISCLOSURE-device; ANCHOR or *-absence).
verbatim.face_of_the_evidence: X2 (lane 02): an MT-borne device (mark, paseq, K/Q, note, formula membership) is cited on the oshb: face; a WEB quotation on the web: face; inside the ch 20/21 zone every entry is dual as already ruled. Outside the zone this is a deterministic re-face (identity numbering) and runs as a MECHANICAL sweep with a distinct check; the two rows lane 02 names as inverting near/far in prose (P11-001, P11-013) are in the prose pass.
verbatim.retro_qualification: The 'existing entries are NOT re-tokenised' clause is amended for ONE deterministic case: every WARRANT-onset and WARRANT-close token this wave installed receives its derived face qualifier by a mechanical sweep (derivable from verse and span; adds information; changes no claim), distinct-checked. WARRANT-rival tokens receive the qualifier and seam pair in the author repair batch (author work: the seam must be read off the SRA). Pre-wave descriptive entries are still not re-tokenised.
verbatim.why_a_qualifier_and_not_a_split_token: a split (WARRANT-onset-near / WARRANT-onset-far) doubles the vocabulary and still leaves the rival unsaid; a qualifier the member verifies is smaller and auditable.
